title: The Chargers We Keep Recommending Are All on Sale
gist: Affiliate deals post on Anker's sitewide Halloween sale (20% off with code HALLOWEEN20 through November 1), framing Anker as the dominant pick across nearly every WIRED charging buying guide. Notable details: discounts of 20-35% on core chargers and power stations, and Labubu blind-box bundles as a crossover marketing play.

insights.claim: Anker wins the top recommendation in nearly every WIRED charging buying guide, including portable chargers, Android chargers, wireless, 3-in-1, MagSafe and USB car chargers.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Editorial dominance across review guides is a durable affiliate-traffic and brand moat for Anker in consumer charging.
insights.quote: Anker is like the Meryl Streep of charging, sweeping the top awards of nearly every charging-related guide

insights.claim: Anker's Halloween sale offers 20 percent off sitewide via code through November 1, with the Nano Charger 45W cut from $40 to $26 (35% off) and the Solix C1000 power station from $600 to $470.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Deep pre-holiday discounting on charging hardware signals competitive pricing pressure in the accessory market.

insights.claim: The author argues demand for chargers is lifted seasonally by forecast storms and more time spent indoors on battery-draining phone use.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Weather-driven outage risk is a seasonal demand driver for power banks and portable power stations.

insights.claim: Anker's Laptop Power Bank packs 25,000 mAh and up to 165 watts across two devices while staying below airline power-capacity limits, making it travel-friendly.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Airline capacity limits cap power bank design, shaping product specs around ~25,000 mAh.

insights.claim: Anker is bundling Labubu blind boxes with popular chargers in its Halloween sale, though the author questions whether the Labubu craze has already faded.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Hardware brands borrowing collectible-toy hype is a signal of how long the Labubu fad's commercial tail runs.
insights.quote: Forgive me, but are Labubus still a thing?
